definitions.gloss: halftone dot; the dot pattern used in halftone printing
definitions.explanation: In printing, the array of tiny dots of varying size that reproduces continuous tones and shades of gray or color. Because ink cannot vary in density on the page, larger or denser dots read as darker areas and smaller ones as lighter.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}は{網点|あみてん}で{印刷|いんさつ}される。
examples.english: Photographs are printed using halftone dots.

examples.japanese: {網点|あみてん}が{粗|あら}いと{画像|がぞう}がぼやけて{見|み}える。
examples.english: When the halftone dots are coarse, the image looks blurred.

examples.japanese: {印刷物|いんさつぶつ}を{拡大鏡|かくだいきょう}で{見|み}ると、{細|こま}かい{網点|あみてん}が{確認|かくにん}できる。
examples.english: Under a magnifier you can make out the fine halftone dots in printed matter.

notes:
Formed from {網|あみ} (net, mesh) + {点|てん} (dot). A basic term in printing and graphic design.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {網点|あみてん}の{密度|みつど}: dot density
- {網点|あみてん}を{使|つか}う: to use a halftone screen

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {階調|かいちょう}: gradation, tone — the range of light-to-dark that halftone dots are used to reproduce.
